Hi, sorry for the delay on this. The issue is indeed that `from_dlpack` is returning a jax.Array with a non-default layout, which jax doesn't handle well yet (jax currently always produces arrays with a default layout, except in this dlpack case). I think Peter was getting at this, but basically even though the array "knows" its own layout, jax assumes all arrays have the default layout, and under the hood is passing this array as input to a jit-compiled code that thinks the input is in the default layout (sometimes jax uses jit-compiled code to implement things like slicing).

The short-term fix is to at least raise an error when passing the wrong layout to a compiled executable. This will cause the print to fail with a probably confusing error :( But at least it won't return wrong results. (I have to look more into exactly what's going on with the print but that's the idea.)

We could also make it an error to even create such an array, like Peter suggests. I think that's probably a good idea until we have better support for non-defeault layouts.

The longer-term fix is better support for non-default layouts, which I'm (slowly) working on.

@tomatillos thanks for reporting this and for the very clear repro btw!

The current state of the issue is as follows (using jax 0.5.1.dev20250129+8c02731a0):
```python
import numpy as np
from jax import dlpack as jdp

a = np.arange(4).reshape(2,2)
b = a.T

print(b)
# [[0 2]
#  [1 3]]

print(b[0,1])
# 2

b_jax = jdp.from_dlpack(b)
# CUDA: AssertionError: Unexpected XLA layout override: (XLA) DeviceLocalLayout(major_to_minor=(0, 1), _tiling=(), _sub_byte_element_size_in_bits=0) != DeviceLocalLayout(major_to_minor=(1, 0), _tiling=(), _sub_byte_element_size_in_bits=0) (User input layout)
# CPU: 2025-02-10 22:15:23.604141: W external/xla/xla/python/dlpack.cc:347] DLPack buffer is not aligned (data at: 0x5630bb2fbed0). Creating a copy.

print(b_jax)
# [[0 2]
#  [1 3]]

print(b_jax[0,1])
# when jax platform is CUDA, see AssertionError above
# when jax platform is CPU, the output is 2
```

That is, the issue as reported is fixed.

Thanks for the comment here, @pearu! I recently updated the CPU client to support layouts (hence why there is no error raised here), but I was under the impression that the GPU version should also work here.

@yashk2810, @ezhulenev — Doesn't the GPU client support user-defined layouts? Do you know why we would still see the assertion error above with the nightly jaxlib?
It seems to be working for me at HEAD on CPU and GPU. Try with the latest nightly?
I confirm that the example code above works both on CPU and GPU when using the current HEAD (jax 0.5.1.dev20250210+b7d012281).
I'm going to close this as fixed because I believe that JAX's DLPack APIs now properly support arbitrary (compact) strides on CPU and GPU.

### Description

When using `from_dlpack` on an array with non-standard strides, JAX returns the wrong arrays (silently). 

Think it's similar to issues mentioned before #4196, #7657, #8082. I understand it might not be possible to do no copy here, but I think it would be best if it raised an error, rather than silently creating the wrong array.

eg:
```
import numpy as np
from jax import dlpack as jdp

a = np.arange(4).reshape(2,2)
b = a.T

print(b)
# [[0 2]
#  [1 3]]

print(b[0,1])
# 2

b_jax = jdp.from_dlpack(b.__dlpack__())

print(b_jax)
# [[0 1]
#  [2 3]]

print(b_jax[0,1])
# 1
```

issue.body:
When using the jax.dlpack interface with strided&transposed arrays I'm getting wrong values when indexing, whereas printing gives the correct array structure.

I think this is similar to #4196 and as explained by @zhangqiaorjc  https://github.com/google/jax/issues/4196#issuecomment-689680107, but here no explicit error is thrown. Also doing a deepcopy with `jax2torch(a.clone())` or `jax2torch(copy.deepcopy(a))` does not seem to help in this case.

In my use-case `a` is expected to come from a longer torch pipeline I don't have control over, so I can't defer transpositions/slices to the JAX side. Are there other workarounds I could try?

mwe:
```python
import torch
import jax
import jax.dlpack
import torch.utils.dlpack
from jax.config import config
config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

def jax2torch(x):
    return torch.utils.dlpack.from_dlpack(jax.dlpack.to_dlpack(x))

def torch2jax(x):
    return jax.dlpack.from_dlpack(torch.utils.dlpack.to_dlpack(x))

a = torch.arange(6).reshape(2,3).moveaxis(1,0)
b = torch2jax(a)

print("stride", a.stride())
# stride (1, 3)

print(a)
# tensor([[0, 3],
#         [1, 4],
#         [2, 5]])

print(b) # these do match
# [[0 3]
#  [1 4]
#  [2 5]]

print(a[1,0], b[1,0]) # these do not match
# tensor(1) 2

print(torch.__version__) # '1.9.0+cpu'
print(jax.__version__) # '0.2.19'
```

issue.body:
## Summary

- The macOS Metal zero-copy capture path (`shared/native-ipc/ipc_apple_torch.cpp`) linked the full libtorch C++ distribution just to hand back a `torch.Tensor` directly instead of a raw DLPack `PyCapsule` from `initialize_from_mach_port()`. The Python caller already knows how to wrap a capsule via `torch.utils.dlpack.from_dlpack(...)` (this is exactly what the CUDA branch already does).
- Removed `ipc_apple_torch.cpp`, all `find_package(Torch)` / `HAS_TORCH` / libtorch-link CMake logic (top-level `CMakeLists.txt` and `tests/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`), and the `curl libtorch... && sudo mv .../libtorch` steps from `cmake-build.yml`, `publish-package-nocuda.yml`, and `gradle.yml` (the last one was dead — the mc121 Gradle/JVM build never used libtorch at all).
- Updated `initialize_zerocopy()` in `observation_converter.py` to wrap the returned capsule with `torch.utils.dlpack.from_dlpack(...)` on the Python side.
- Fixed `convert_jax_observation()`'s Apple branch, which imported a `mtl_dlpack_from_mach_port` symbol that never existed in the native module (dead import, would have raised `ImportError` if ever exercised) — now uses `initialize_from_mach_port`, which returns the same raw DLPack capsule.

## Why

This also fixes the macOS build breakage seen in CI and in a local release-wheel dry run: libtorch 2.5.1's `c10/util/strong_type.h` specializes `std::is_arithmetic`, which newer Xcode/libc++ (SDK 26.x, shipped on GitHub's `macos-26` runner that `macos-latest` is migrating to) marks with `_LIBCPP_NO_SPECIALIZATIONS`, causing a hard compile error:

```
error: 'is_arithmetic' cannot be specialized: Users are not allowed to specialize this standard library entity [-Winvalid-specialization]
```

Verified locally (SDK header diff) that MacOSX15.4.sdk (Xcode 16.4, current `macos-15` default) doesn't have this restriction but MacOSX26.5.sdk does — so this was a real, if latent, incompatibility waiting to surface as GitHub rolls `macos-latest` forward. Removing the libtorch dependency avoids the problem entirely instead of just pinning around it, and drops a large, narrowly-used native dependency plus its associated build steps.

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake -B build_tests -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -S .` + `cmake --build build_tests` — clean build on macOS with no libtorch installed at all
- [x] `ctest` in `build_tests` — `IPCModuleTest.AddFunction` passes
- [x] `pip wheel . --no-deps` (scratch venv, Python 3.14) — builds a wheel successfully with no libtorch present, confirming the macOS `is_arithmetic` failure is gone
- [ ] CI (this PR) — cmake-build, gradle, and wheel-build workflows should now pass on macOS without the libtorch install step
